issues.legal_issue: A finding that a landlord bona fide requires additional accommodation for the household is not perverse merely because the landlord understated the number of rooms, the household has managed to share rooms, or there is no evidence that adult family members will marry imminently, where the actual accommodation and household needs support the finding.
material_facts: The landlord lived in the house with his wife, a married son and the son's wife, three adult unmarried sons, and a daughter.
A court-appointed commissioner inspected the house and reported on the number, use, and small dimensions of the rooms available to the landlord.
The trial court found that the married couple occupied one room and the three adult sons shared another, leaving inadequate space for the household; the appellate court independently agreed.
The High Court reversed the concurrent findings, relying in part on the landlord's failure to state the full number of rooms and the absence of evidence of imminent marriages.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent finding of bona fide need for additional accommodation was supported by the evidence and was not perverse; the High Court was not justified in reversing it.
issues.legal_principle: A second appellate court should not set aside concurrent factual findings as perverse when the evidence, including an inspection of the actual accommodation and the household's needs, supports them. The assessment of bona fide need must consider the size and use of the rooms, privacy and convenience, and the household as a whole; proof of imminent marriages is not required in these circumstances. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.second_appeal_from_concurrent_eviction_f: The matter is a second appeal from concurrent findings in an eviction suit.
predicates.landlord_seeks_additional_family_space: The landlord seeks possession of leased space to provide additional accommodation for the household.
predicates.inspected_rooms_are_inadequate_for_house: An inspection shows that the rooms available to the household are too small or insufficient for its members and their reasonable living needs.
predicates.findings_are_supported_by_evidence: The courts' factual findings are supported by evidence about the accommodation and the household.

issues.definition: When a second appeal challenges concurrent eviction findings, an evidence-supported finding that inspected accommodation is inadequate for a household seeking additional family space stands.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant sublets leased premises without the landlord's consent when the tenant permanently leaves and gives the premises over to a relative for that relative's occupation; the relative's status as a family member does not by itself make the occupation a licence.
material_facts: The tenant admitted that he had moved his residence elsewhere and was no longer occupying the leased rooms.
The tenant's brother occupied the rooms left by the tenant.
The tenant had given the rooms to his brother without the landlord's consent.
The trial court and appellate court found that the tenant had permanently surrendered possession of the rooms.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established unauthorised subletting, and the High Court was not justified in setting aside the concurrent findings on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Where the tenant has permanently shifted elsewhere and left the leased premises entirely to another person, the other person's occupation is not merely a licence arising from kinship. The court applied the rule against unauthorised subletting; no provision or earlier case is specifically cited for this issue.

rule.if: eviction_proceeding_for_unauthorised_subletting and tenant_permanently_left_premises and another_person_has_occupation and landlord_did_not_consent

predicates.eviction_proceeding_for_unauthorised_sub: The proceeding seeks eviction on the ground that the tenant sublet the premises without permission.
predicates.tenant_permanently_left_premises: The tenant ceased residing in the leased premises and shifted elsewhere permanently.
predicates.another_person_has_occupation: Another person was left in occupation of the leased premises by the tenant.
predicates.landlord_did_not_consent: The landlord did not consent to that person's occupation.

issues.definition: Unauthorised subletting is established when, in an eviction proceeding on that ground, a tenant permanently leaves the premises and another person occupies them without the landlord's consent.

issues.legal_issue: The requirement that a landlord not possess reasonably suitable alternative accommodation may not strictly apply when the landlord already occupies part of a house and seeks the leased portion as additional space for the household.
material_facts: The landlord occupied part of the house and sought possession of the leased portion to meet the household's additional accommodation needs.
The landlord owned another house several miles away, but evidence showed that it was occupied by tenants and no part was vacant.
The trial and appellate courts found the landlord's need for additional accommodation established.
issues.conclusion: The existence of the other, fully tenanted house did not defeat the claim; in a claim for additional accommodation within the house already occupied by the landlord, the alternative-accommodation condition in Section 13 need not be strictly applied.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13, including Section 13(ff) as invoked for possession for the landlord's own occupation, the condition that the landlord not possess reasonably suitable accommodation may not be strictly attracted where the landlord already occupies part of a house and seeks the leased portion as additional accommodation. The court also relied on the evidence that the other house was fully occupied by tenants. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.eviction_proceeding_for_additional_famil: The proceeding seeks possession of leased space to provide additional accommodation for the landlord's household.
predicates.landlord_already_occupies_part_of_home: The landlord and the household already occupy part of the home containing the leased premises.
predicates.leased_space_is_sought_as_additional_spa: The landlord seeks the leased portion to add space to the household's existing accommodation.
predicates.other_property_is_not_vacant: Other property owned by the landlord is occupied by others and has no vacant portion available.

issues.definition: A landlord's other property does not defeat a claim for additional household space when the landlord already occupies part of the home and the other property is not vacant.

issues.legal_issue: A remand is unnecessary to determine whether alternative accommodation is available when, despite the absence of a formally framed issue, the parties tried the case and adduced evidence on that matter.
material_facts: No formal issue was framed on the availability of alternative accommodation.
The parties nevertheless went to trial with that matter in mind and adduced evidence about the other house and its occupation by tenants.
The evidence showed that no portion of the other house was vacant.
issues.conclusion: The appeal did not need to be remanded for a finding on the availability of alternative suitable accommodation.
issues.legal_principle: A matter need not be remanded for a finding merely because no formal issue was framed if the parties understood that it was in dispute, adduced evidence on it, and placed that evidence before the court. No provision or earlier case is cited for this procedural ruling.

predicates.eviction_appeal_involving_alternative_ac: The appeal raises whether alternative accommodation is available to the landlord in an eviction proceeding.
predicates.no_formal_issue_was_framed: The trial court did not formally frame an issue on alternative accommodation.
predicates.parties_tried_the_alternative_accommodat: The parties proceeded on the understanding that alternative accommodation was in dispute.
predicates.evidence_was_adduced_on_it: The parties presented evidence addressing the availability and occupation of the alleged alternative accommodation.

issues.definition: A remand is unnecessary when the parties tried and presented evidence on alternative accommodation even though no formal issue was framed.
